purpose: My personal MPC studies, practice, creations, and discoveries. Other people may read the notebook, but my musical goals and development determine its direction.
method: Start with something to hear or do, not a menu to memorize. Each assignment develops one useful skill through a small musical experiment.
Predict, act, listen, explain, vary, and keep the result. Try independently first; open the control hints when needed. A surprising result is information, not a failed lesson.
Use my own material and musical choices. No assigned genre, chord progression, or compositional formula. Compare a result before deciding what I prefer.
Teach useful prerequisites proactively: preserving work before risky editing, selection scope before sound design, routing before adding devices. Credit existing ability with a brief demonstration.

Practice correctness, then recovery, then fewer unnecessary actions. Revisit a skill in a later session and with different material. The suggested times are flexible practice blocks, not mastery deadlines.
Record the sound or practical result, one observation, and one next experiment. Separate New, Practiced, Reliable, and Ready to perform; a checkbox or one guided attempt does not establish mastery.
